the extent of ornithine decaboxylase (ODA) induction by 12-O-tetradeconolylphorbol-13-acetate in the female Sprague-Dewley rat is dependent on the route, dose, time and exposure of the administration.
the extent of ODC induction by TPA depended on the dose and time of administration, the route of administration and the time after administration.
12-O-tetradeacanoylphobol 13-acetat (TPA) induced ornithine decaboxylase (ODA) activity, the key regulatory enzyme in polyamine metabolism, in a dose-, time-, and route-dependent manner.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dose, time, route and duration dependency of TPA induction of hepatic ODC in rats.
the effects of the phorbol ester, TPA, on the activity of ODC, a key enzyme in polyamine metabolism, in rat liver.
the dose, route, time and exposure dependency of the induction by TPA of rat hepatic ODC.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the induction of ODC activity in liver by TPA is a dose, time and route dependent phenomenon and that TPA has no adverse effects on the liver.
TPA is an effective inducer of hepatic ODC activity in rats and is not a hepatotoxin.
TPA induced ODC in a dose and time dependent manner, but was non-toxic at doses which induced ODC.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
TPA is a potent inducer of ODC in rats, and that the induction is dependent on dose, exposure and route of administration.
ODC induction in vivo is dose, time and route dependent.
ODC is a useful marker for the study of TPA-induced carcinogenesis in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
ODC is a useful biomarker for TPA exposure in rats.
ODC induction is a sensitive marker for the detection of TPA exposure.
